children: , the American memory-chip producer, fell approximately 4.2% to $984.62 Thursday even as a global high-bandwidth-memory crunch gave suppliers more pricing power. Chinese AI-chip companies raised prices as scarce HBM supplies pushed component costs higher, with Huawei's upcoming Ascend accelerator reportedly becoming 20% to 50% more expensive.

Micron's fiscal third-quarter results show just how dramatically that scarcity is flowing through the business. Revenue surged to $41.46 billion from $9.30 billion a year earlier, while adjusted free cash flow reached $18.3 billion. Management expects approximately $50 billion in fourth-quarter revenue and an adjusted gross margin near 86%.

That forecast implies another 20.6% sequential revenue jump, while third-quarter adjusted free cash flow represented a remarkable 44.1% of sales. Yet the chart flashes a clear valuation warning: Micron's $984.62 share price stands 56.92% above its GF Value estimate of $627.48. The shortage is delivering extraordinary economics, but the premium leaves little room for AI demandor memory pricingto cool.

title: Micron Drops 4.2% While China's AI Chips Reveal Its Pricing Power
